newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk actor on trial for Kafka's "Trial" recital.
newsitem.headline: Turk actor on trial for Kafka's "Trial" recital.

text.p: A Turkish actor faces up to three years in jail for reciting a passage of Franz Kafka's novel "The Trial" in court to judges trying him for deliberately flouting freedom of expression laws, the actor said on Friday.
Mahir Gunsiray appeared in an Istanbul court on Thursday accused of "insulting the bench" for reading aloud a section of the Czech's famous novel in a State Security Court in March.
The book details the nightmarish journey through a repressive legal system of an ordinary man who is never aware of the charges against him.
Gunsiray had originally been on trial with almost 100 other people who had published a banned book to draw attention to Turkey's freedom of expression laws. That trial is continuing.
He quoted a Turkish translation from the German of "The Trial" in which the hero, Josef, questions his accusers on their right to judge him.

"It was such a comical, absurd situation that I read them Kafka," Gunsiray told Reuters. "The judges asked me twice if this was meant as a verbal attack on them and I said it wasn't. I just wanted to read out the passage," he said.
Gunsiray also quoted Don Quixote's self-effacing companion Sancho Panza in his defence on Thursday. The case was adjourned until December.
Turkey's restrictions on written dissent, mostly used against Kurdish activists, have often been criticised in the West.
